content.title: Livvy Dunne
content.text: From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia Livvy DunneDunne with the LSU Tigers in 2025Personal informationFull nameOlivia Paige DunneNickname(s)Livvy, LivBornOctober 1, 2002 (age 23)Westwood, New Jersey, U.S.Height5 ft 6.25 in (168 cm)Gymnastics careerDisciplineWomen's artistic gymnasticsCountryrepresented United States (2017)College teamLSU Tigers (2021–2025)ClubENA ParamusHead coach(es)Jay ClarkRetiredApril 17, 2025Medal record Representing Louisiana State Tigers NCAA Championships 2024 Fort Worth Team TikTok informationPagelivvyFollowers7.9 million (January 27, 2026) Olivia Paige Dunne (born October 1, 2002) is an American influencer and former artistic gymnast. She is also a Sports Illustrated swimsuit model and former member of the LSU Tigers women's gymnastics team. In 2017, she was named as a member of the US Junior Women's National Team.[1] Dunne has a social media following of over 10 million.[2] Dunne was born on October 1, 2002, in Westwood, New Jersey, and grew up in Hillsdale, New Jersey.[3] She started her gymnastics training in 2005 at ENA Gymnastics[4] in Paramus, New Jersey.[5] By the time she was 14 years old, Dunne was homeschooled by her mother, using the Abeka Academy curriculum,[6] while she spent her days training with her coach Craig Zappa at ENA Gymnastics.[7] Dunne made her elite debut at the 2014 American Classic where she finished 28th in the all-around.[8] She next competed at the U.S. Classic where she placed 12th in the all-around.[9] In 2015, Dunne re-qualified for elite status at the WOGA Classic, where she earned a qualifying score of 52.750 and placed fifth.[10] She next competed at the American Classic where she placed eighth and qualified to compete at the 2015 National Championships.[11] Dunne competed at the U.S. Classic where she placed 24th in the last round.[12] Dunne made her National Championships debut in 2015 where she placed 25th in the all-around.[13] Dunne competed at the 2016 American Classic where she finished 27th in the all-around.[14] She next competed at the 2016 U.S. Classic where she finished 24th.[15] Dunne concluded the season competing at the 2016 National Championships where she finished 12th in the all-around. She also placed eighth on balance beam and sixth on floor exercise.[16] In March 2017, Dunne was selected for the team to compete at the 2017 City of Jesolo Trophy; as a result she was added to the National Team for the first time.[17] She made her international debut there and placed sixth in the all-around.[18] Dunne competed at the 2017 U.S. Classic in July where she finished fifth in the all-around.[19] At the 2017 National Championships, Dunne finished ninth in the all-around.[20] Dunne turned senior in 2018. Although the United States did not send a team, Dunne represented her club at the 2018 City of Jesolo Trophy. She finished 15th in the all-around.[21] She competed at the 2018 U.S. Classic only on uneven bars due to an ankle injury.[22] Dunne qualified to compete at the National Championships via petition.[23] She ended up placing 18th in the all-around.[24] Having not competed during the 2019 season in order to rest her injuries,[25] Dunne officially signed her National Letter of Intent with Louisiana State University in November, starting in the 2020–21 season.[26] Dunne qualified to the 2020 Nastia Liukin Cup after dropping down to Level 10.[27] She ended up placing 11th.[28] Dunne performing with the LSU Tigers, 2024 Dunne joined the LSU Tigers gymnastics team in 2020. During the 2020–21 season, she competed on the uneven bars in every regular-season meet.[29] She made her NCAA debut in a meet against Arkansas, scoring 9.875.[30] She entered the postseason with an NQS of 9.9 on bars.[31] At the SEC Championships, she contributed an uneven bars score of 9.9 to LSU's second-place team finish.[32] At the NCAA Championships semi-finals, she again scored 9.9 on bars; LSU did not advance to the finals.[33] The next season, Dunne again competed on the uneven bars in every regular-season meet and also competed five times on the floor exercise. She matched her career-high of 9.925 on the uneven bars during the opening meet against Centenary.[34] She earned a score of 9.800 in her collegiate debut on floor on January 28.[35] At the SEC Championships, she contributed an uneven bars score of 9.875, but LSU was forced to count a fall on that event and finished in fifth place overall.[36] At the NCAA regional semifinals, she contributed scores of 9.85 on uneven bars and 9.9 on floor exercise.[37] LSU suffered two uncharacteristic falls on balance beam and as a result was eliminated from the postseason during the first round of regionals, failing to qualify for the national championship as a team for the first time since 2011. After missing much of the 2022–23 season due to various injuries including two torn labrums, a torn bicep,[38] and a stress reaction in her leg,[39] Dunne made her season debut on February 24 against Alabama, scoring a 9.825 on the uneven bars. During the 2023–24 season, Dunne competed eight routines on floor exercise, matching her career-high of 9.9 twice.[40] She also competed on the uneven bars twice, including at the SEC Championships, where LSU won the team title.[41] At the NCAA Championships, the Tigers won their first national championship title in program history.[42] Dunne confirmed that she intended to take her fifth year of eligibility that the COVID-19 pandemic had granted NCAA athletes.[43][44] She competed in the first four meets of the 2024–2025 season before sustaining an avulsion fracture in her kneecap, ending her NCAA career.[45][46] Dunne announced her retirement from gymnastics on April 17, 2025.[47][48] In March 2026, Dunne was cast in a recurring role as Grace in a Baywatch reboot.[49] Dunne joined the social media platform TikTok in 2020. Initially she posted videos of her gymnastics but later started posting videos of other areas of her life as well.[50] As of February 2023, Dunne is the most-followed NCAA athlete on social media, with more than 8 million followers on TikTok and 5 million on Instagram. On July 2, 2021, the NCAA changed its rule to allow its athletes to earn money from their name, image, and likeness (NIL).[51] Dunne was projected to earn more than any other collegiate athlete due to her large social-media platform, which was a combined five million followers across both Instagram and TikTok at the time of the rule change.[52] In August, Dunne announced that she signed with WME Sports, becoming their first NIL athlete.[53] A month later, she announced her first exclusive brand partnership with activewear brand Vuori.[54] As of May 2023, Dunne was the highest-valued women's college athlete with an estimated NIL valuation of $3.3 million,[55] which led to endorsement deals with Grubhub, Vuori, Bodyarmor, and American Eagle Outfitters. In February 2023, she stated during an appearance on the morning program Today that her endorsement deals total seven figures.[2] On January 6, 2023, a large group of fans showed up to LSU's opening meet of the season at Utah to support Dunne. Some of these fans were reportedly harassing members of both gymnastics teams as well as journalists both during and after the meet. As a result of this, LSU hired additional security staff for the team and implemented increased safety measures including disallowing LSU gymnasts to go into the stands after a meet. Following the incident, Dunne posted a statement to Twitter requesting that her fans be more respectful.[56] On February 27, 2023, Dunne posted a paid-sponsorship video to TikTok promoting Caktus.AI with the caption, "Needing to get my creativity flowing for my essay due at midnight". The video showed her generating an essay using the service, with the camera then panning to show a shocked expression on the star, concluding with the caption "Caktus.AI > ChatGPT".[57] LSU issued a statement saying, "At LSU, our professors and students are empowered to use technology for learning and pursuing the highest standards of academic integrity. However, using AI to produce work that a student then represents as one's own could result in a charge of academic misconduct, as outlined in the Code of Student Conduct."[58] In July 2023, Dunne revealed that she had received more than $500,000 for a single social media post online.[59] Later that month, Dunne announced that she had partnered with Bayou Traditions to launch The Livvy Fund, a program that will connect female student athletes at LSU with top brands to secure NIL endorsement deals.[60] Dunne was featured in the 2023 and 2024 editions of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue.[61] For the 2025 edition she was selected as one of four cover models alongside Lauren Chan, Salma Hayek, and fellow gymnast Jordan Chiles.[62] In 2024 Dunne was added to the Forbes 30 under 30 list.[63] In 2025, Dunne was named in Time magazine’s inaugural “TIME100 Creators” list - branded by the publication as the 100 most influential digital voices. [64] Dunne is dating professional baseball pitcher Paul Skenes, a former player for the LSU baseball team.[65] She was in attendance for his debut with the Pittsburgh Pirates in 2024.[66] Dunne was featured on The Money Game: LSU, a six-part NIL-focused docuseries by Prime Video that followed her, Jayden Daniels, Angel Reese, Flau'jae Johnson, Alia Armstrong, and Trace Young through LSU's 2023–24 sports season.[67] The series was nominated for Outstanding Documentary Series (Serialized) at the 46th Sports Emmy Awards.[68] Competitive history[edit] Competitive history of Olivia Dunne Year Event Team AA VT UB BB FX 2014 American Classic 28 31 25 16 18 U.S. Classic 33 36 35 29 20 2015 WOGA Classic 5 American Classic 8 18 15 9 6 U.S. Classic 24 34 30 14 12 U.S. National Championships 25 27 23 23 21 2016 American Classic 27 26 26 22 20 U.S. Classic 24 33 23 20 13 U.S. National Championships 12 22 21 8 6 2017 City of Jesolo Trophy 6 American Classic 12 6 U.S. Classic 5 22 11 6 6 U.S. National Championships 9 15 9 7 8 2018 City of Jesolo Trophy 15 U.S. Classic 15 U.S. National Championships 18 17 20 19 2020 Nastia Liukin Cup 11 2021 SEC Championships 5 NCAA Championships 6 9 2022 SEC Championships 5 17 2023 SEC Championships 28 2024 SEC Championships 41 NCAA Championships List of television shows, showing year aired, character played and notes Year TV show Role Notes Ref. 2024 The Money Game: LSU Herself Main role (Season 1–present) ^ "Past Women's Junior National Teams • USA Gymnastics".
